title: Two Sum
prompt:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indexes [i, j] (with i < j) of the two numbers that add up to target. You may not use the same element twice. If no pair exists, return []. Each test input has at most one valid pair.

Write twoSum(nums, target).

  • twoSum([320, 150, 410, 180, 60], 500) → [0, 3]
  • twoSum([2, 7, 11, 15], 9) → [0, 1]
  • twoSum([3, 3], 6) → [0, 1]
  • twoSum([1, 2], 7) → []

Constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 10^5, values may be negative. The array is not sorted. Aim for O(n) time.

tests.name: finds the pair of page counts
duplicate values can form the pair
an element cannot pair with itself
no pair or too few elements returns []

hints: Trigger: an unsorted array and a pair that sums to a target. The brute force inner loop searches for one specific value.
Idea: for nums[i], the partner it needs is target - nums[i]. Keep a Map of every value you have already passed to the index where you saw it, and ask it for the partner.
Code shape: for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) { const need = target - nums[i]; if (map.has(need)) return [map.get(need), i]; map.set(nums[i], i); }. Check first, then add.
explain:
Time O(n), space O(n). One pass; each step does an O(1) map lookup and insert. The brute force was O(n²) because, for every element, it scanned the rest of the array looking for its complement; the map replaces that scan with one lookup.

How to say it: "For each number I know exactly which partner I need, target minus it. I keep a map from value to index of what I've seen, so finding the partner is O(1). One pass, O(n) time, O(n) space. If the array were sorted I'd use two pointers instead for O(1) space."
